decisions.reason: The low-noise burner strengthens the firm's quality and customer-comfort positioning within its established infrared heating business, so it is worth retaining despite limited later visibility.
A gas infrared plaque heater fits the firm's core offer for large commercial and industrial spaces and its own product page suggests it was important enough to keep as a main line.
The gas infrared luminous radiant heater had only brief launch visibility and is a less compelling fit with the firm's efficiency and CO2-reduction positioning than its other core heater types.
Gas-fired infrared tube heaters are a standard core solution for halls and industrial buildings, so keeping one such line supports the firm's main market focus.
The standard gas infrared plaque heater overlaps strongly with the other plaque-heater offer and adds too little differentiation to justify splitting resources.
This tube-heater offer appears redundant with the other gas-fired infrared tube heater and, with no sustained web prominence, is best removed in a portfolio cleanup.
